title: Extension by zero on a ringed-site slice preserves and reflects exactness
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $U\in\mathcal C$. Use the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ and restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $j_{U!}\mathcal G=(P_{\mathcal G})^\#$, where $P_{\mathcal G}$ is the direct-sum extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and $(-)^\#$ is module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every complex $\mathcal G_1\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal G_2\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal G_3$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules ($b\circ a=0$), one has $\operatorname{im}(a)=\ker(b)$ if and only if $\operatorname{im}(j_{U!}a)=\ker(j_{U!}b)$ in the category of $\mathcal O$-modules.

proof.text: Write $J=j_{U!}$. The cited ringed-site adjunction lemma gives that $J$ is exact for the very sheafified direct-sum construction in the statement. Thus, if $\operatorname{im}(a)=\ker(b)$, applying $J$ preserves this equality: kernels are finite limits, cokernels are finite colimits, and the image of $a$ is the kernel of its cokernel. This proves the forward implication without assuming that epimorphisms are surjective on sections.

For any $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal G$ define $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to (J\mathcal G)|_U$ as follows. At $(V,\varphi:V\to U)$ send $s$ into the $\varphi$-summand of $P_{\mathcal G}(V)$ and then into its sheafification. Under $h:V^{\prime}\to V$ this summand maps to the $\varphi h$-summand, so the maps commute with restriction and are module-linear. Suppose $\eta_{\mathcal G}(s)=0$. The module sheafification interface identifies its underlying abelian sheaf with abelian sheafification; the underlying-sets comparison therefore permits the local-equality criterion for set sheafification. There is a cover $\{h_i:V_i\to V\}$ on which the element supported in the $\varphi h_i$-summand is zero in $P_{\mathcal G}(V_i)$. Inclusion into a direct sum is injective (project back to that coordinate), so $s|_{(V_i,\varphi h_i)}=0$. These maps cover $(V,\varphi)$ in the localized topology; separatedness of the sheaf $\mathcal G$ gives $s=0$. Consequently $\eta_{\mathcal G}$ is sectionwise injective, hence a monomorphism. This also works for an empty cover, because a sheaf has only the zero section on an object covered by the empty family.

proof.text: The preceding injection detects zero objects: if $J\mathcal H=0$, restriction is zero sectionwise, so the injection $\eta_{\mathcal H}:\mathcal H\to (J\mathcal H)|_U=0$ forces every section of $\mathcal H$ to vanish, hence $\mathcal H=0$. No assertion that the unit is an isomorphism is needed.

For the converse put $\mathcal K=\ker(b)$ and let $\bar a:\mathcal G_1\to\mathcal K$ be the factorization of $a$ (which exists because $ba=0$). Let $\mathcal H=\operatorname{coker}(\bar a)$, so the original complex is exact precisely when $\mathcal H=0$. Exactness of $J$ identifies $J\mathcal K$ with $\ker(Jb)$, identifies $J\bar a$ with the factorization of $Ja$ through that kernel, and identifies $J\mathcal H$ with its cokernel. If the extended complex is exact, that factorization is an epimorphism, so $J\mathcal H=0$. Step 3 gives $\mathcal H=0$, and hence $\operatorname{im}(a)=\ker(b)$.
